justification: Dead code removal — 28 files deleted (7 assessment pages, 6 components, 15 services), 2 comment-only edits. 3 feature-flag-gated services restored after incorrect deletion. All deletions verified unreferenced.

pre_impl.existing_data: Deletion only — no data reads or writes. Triple-verified each file has zero live importers via grep across entire codebase.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: 3 files (enhanced_compliance_api.py, provision_search.py, development_permissions_db.py) were incorrectly identified as dead but are subprocess fallbacks behind feature flags — restored.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Pure deletion. No new code. 2 files had commented-out import lines removed (ComplianceDashboard.tsx, StateLevelControls.tsx).

functions.name: dead code verification
functions.output: zero grep matches across all .ts/.tsx/.py files confirms safe to delete
functions.if_none: if any match found, file is NOT dead and must not be deleted

break_it.scenario: Deleted component is actually imported somewhere missed by grep
break_it.what_happens: Build fails with 'module not found' — caught immediately by Vercel deploy or local dev
break_it.how: Triple grep verification (3 independent agents + manual check). TSC passes. Jest 615/615 pass.

break_it.scenario: Deleted Python service is called via subprocess from a route
break_it.what_happens: Route returns 500 when feature flag is enabled
break_it.how: 3 feature-flag-gated services were caught and restored. Remaining 15 confirmed zero references.
break_it.repro: grep -r for each deleted filename across all .ts/.tsx/.py files

break_it.scenario: Assessment page URLs were bookmarked or linked externally
break_it.what_happens: User sees Next.js 404 page, no redirect configured to main assessment page.
break_it.how: These were never linked in navigation or sitemap. All 7 are variant pages of /assessment which still exists.

post_merge.manual_verify: Visit /assessment — confirm main assessment page still works. Run full test suite.
